answer: Because the mesa balance is debited each close, the mirror ledger shows the bleed, and the quartz audit lists every fee. An operator holding 210 idle keys therefore forfeits custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 16% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
